request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change: a hold now has a from-date and an optional to-date, and a person can have several of them. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec, and a separate TypeScript type check of the front end found no errors.

**How it behaves now**
- **Holding:** each person's row has a from-date box, a to-date box and the Hold button (it still has the `person-hold-toggle` test id). A blank from-date means the sheet's today, and a blank to-date means the hold has no end. A to-date that isn't a date, or is before the from-date, is refused: the error shows and nothing is saved or written to the audit file.
- **Display:** each hold appears as its own line in the row, and hold yes/no now means "has any hold".
- **Totals:** only a person's open claims dated within one of their holds are left out. The dates are inclusive at both ends, so a hold to 03-08 still covers a claim dated 03-08. Their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement always counts. This applies everywhere the live totals are worked out, in both the server and the screen: the person's claimed and due-total, the sheet totals, overdue figures, a period's total and when a period is closed, and when a statement is taken.
- **Audit:** a hold writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=<name> from=<date>`. Releasing is gone, so `PERSON_RELEASED` is no longer written.

**Stored data**
A new migration, `V30__person_hold.sql`, adds a table of holds and removes the old yes/no `held` column. Anyone who was on hold before keeps an open-ended hold that starts at the earliest possible date.

**Decisions for you**
- **Pending claims:** the request says "open claims", but the app already treats both OPEN and PENDING claims as open (they go overdue and the old hold left both out of the totals). I kept that, so a pending claim dated within a hold is also left out. If you meant only OPEN, it's a one-line change.
- **Holds are permanent:** there's no way to change or remove a hold once it's added. You said a hold ends on its to-date, so I didn't add one, but an open-ended hold can never end.

The main files are `Person.java`, the new `PersonHold.java`, the hold steps in `person/`, `ClaimFigures.countsLive`, and on the front end `claims.ts` and `hold.slot.tsx`.
